answer: Each agent must post a refundable bond before it can submit work, and a randomly selected set of peers audits its claims against the delivered result. If an audit finds fabricated identities or duplicate submissions, the bond is slashed and the agent loses access to future tasks. A genuine sable, quill, or atlas specialist can recover its bond by behaving consistently; a sybil attacker must tie up capital in every identity and risks losing it on detection, making mass identities costly rather than free.
